meta.provenance: Concepts and trap structures derived from KMF/Gremlin's GRE source set; every stem, all numbers, all options, all explanations and all figures are original. No source text or artwork reproduced. Several single-answer sources were recast into numeric-entry and multiple-answer form, since the Coordinate Geometry source pool skews to MCQ and quantitative comparison.

questions.question: In the xy-plane, points J and K have coordinates (9t, -5t) and (-3t, 11t), where t is a nonzero constant. What are the coordinates of the midpoint of segment JK?
questions.explanation: The midpoint averages each coordinate separately. For x: (9t + (-3t))/2 = 6t/2 = 3t. For y: (-5t + 11t)/2 = 6t/2 = 3t. So the midpoint is (3t, 3t). The t does not cancel here, because averaging is an addition, not a ratio.
questions.trap: Students drop the t and answer (3, 3), option A. That would only be the midpoint when t = 1. Unlike a slope, where the common factor divides out top and bottom, a midpoint keeps the factor.

questions.question: In Quadrant I of the xy-plane, a triangle has vertices (k, k), (5k, k) and (k, 4k), where k > 0. If the area of the triangle is 216, what is the value of k?
questions.explanation: Two vertices share the y-value k, so the side joining them is horizontal with length 5k - k = 4k. Two vertices share the x-value k, so that side is vertical with length 4k - k = 3k. The two meet at (k, k) at a right angle, so they are the legs. The area is (1/2)(4k)(3k) = 6k^2. Setting 6k^2 = 216 gives k^2 = 36, and since k > 0, k = 6.
questions.trap: Students multiply the legs without halving, solving 12k^2 = 216 to get k = sqrt(18). The figure is a triangle, not the rectangle its two legs would bound, so the product of the legs must still be halved.

questions.question:
In the xy-plane, the point (c, d) lies below the x-axis and to the left of the y-axis, and c = 3d.
Column A: c
Column B: d
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: Lying below the x-axis makes d negative, and lying left of the y-axis makes c negative. Since c = 3d and d is negative, tripling d pushes it further from zero in the negative direction: if d = -2 then c = -6, and if d = -0.5 then c = -1.5. In every case c is more negative than d, so d is the greater of the two and Column B wins.
questions.trap: Students see the multiplier 3 and conclude c must be the larger, choosing A. Multiplying by 3 enlarges a positive number but shrinks a negative one, because it moves the value further left on the number line.

questions.question:
In the xy-plane, three vertices of a parallelogram are (1, 2), (6, 4) and (3, 8), as shown.

Which of the following could be the fourth vertex?

Indicate all such points.

questions.explanation: Nothing says which of the three given points is opposite the missing one, so all three arrangements are allowed. In a parallelogram the two diagonals share a midpoint, which means the fourth vertex equals the sum of two given vertices minus the third. Taking (1, 2) + (6, 4) - (3, 8) gives (4, -2). Taking (1, 2) + (3, 8) - (6, 4) gives (-2, 6). Taking (6, 4) + (3, 8) - (1, 2) gives (8, 10). Those are the only three possibilities, and options D, E and F are none of them.
questions.trap: Students find one fourth vertex, usually (8, 10), and select it alone. With three unlabelled vertices there is no fixed pairing, so a parallelogram can be completed in three different ways and all three points must be marked.

questions.question:
The figure shows triangle PQR in the xy-plane, with P(5, 2), Q(5, 12) and R(w, 7), where w > 5. Which of the following must be true?

Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
questions.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 260" width="320" height="260" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="a" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="6" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z" fill="#1f2937"/></marker></defs><path d="M76.8 234.0V26.0M118.4 234.0V26.0M160.0 234.0V26.0M201.6 234.0V26.0M243.2 234.0V26.0M62.9 220.1H257.1M62.9 178.5H257.1M62.9 136.9H257.1M62.9 95.3H257.1M62.9 53.7H257.1" stroke="#d7dee8" stroke-width="1" fill="none"/><line x1="62.9" y1="220.1" x2="257.1" y2="220.1" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#a)"/><line x1="76.8" y1="234.0" x2="76.8" y2="26.0" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#a)"/><text x="253.1" y="236.1" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">x</text><text x="83.8" y="37.0" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">y</text><text x="63.8" y="235.1" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">O</text><polygon points="146.1,192.4 146.1,53.7 215.5,123.1" stroke="#1f2937" fill="none" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="146.1" cy="192.4" r="3.5" fill="#1f2937"/><text x="139.1" y="198.4" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937" text-anchor="end">P (5, 2)</text><circle cx="146.1" cy="53.7" r="3.5" fill="#1f2937"/><text x="139.1" y="53.7" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937" text-anchor="end">Q (5, 12)</text><circle cx="215.5" cy="123.1" r="3.5" fill="#1f2937"/><text x="223.5" y="128.1" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">R (w, 7)</text></svg>
options: B. The area of triangle PQR is 50
E. The perimeter of triangle PQR is 40
questions.explanation:
P and Q share the x-value 5, so side PQ is vertical and runs from y = 2 to y = 12, a length of 10. The midpoint of that side sits at y = 7 - exactly the height of R. So R lies on the horizontal line through the midpoint of PQ, which is the perpendicular bisector of PQ. Concretely, RP = sqrt((w - 5)^2 + (7 - 2)^2) and RQ = sqrt((w - 5)^2 + (12 - 7)^2), and both vertical gaps are 5, so the two lengths are identical whatever w is. That makes RP = RQ the one statement true for every allowed w.

Each of the other four pins w down to a single value. RP = PQ needs (w - 5)^2 = 75, that is w = 5 + 5*sqrt(3), about 13.7. The area of PQR is (1/2)(PQ)(w - 5) = 5(w - 5), which equals 50 only when w = 15. RQ is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs w - 5 > 0 and 5, so RQ is always greater than 5 and never equal to it. And the perimeter is 2*RQ + 10, which reaches 40 only when RQ = 15, that is when w = 5 + 10*sqrt(2), about 19.1.
questions.trap: Students pick one convenient value of w, check a statement against it, and stop. A "must be true" item asks for the statement that survives every allowed w, not one that happens to work for a round value, so testing a single w can only eliminate options, never confirm one. Others grab a number straight off the coordinates - reading the vertical gap of 5 from R up to Q as the whole distance RQ, or sizing the area against PQ = 10 as though the horizontal run were 10 as well. Moving R horizontally changes RP and RQ by exactly the same amount, because R stays level with the midpoint of PQ; every other statement on the list turns on where w actually sits.

questions.question:
In the xy-plane, the points (0, -6) and (0, 6) both lie on circle C.
Column A: the radius of circle C
Column B: 6
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: The two given points are 12 units apart, so they form a chord of length 12. A chord can never be longer than a diameter, so the diameter is at least 12 and the radius at least 6. Equality happens only when that chord is itself a diameter, which requires the center to be the origin. But the center is free to sit anywhere on the perpendicular bisector of the chord, the line y = 0. Put the center at (8, 0) and the radius becomes the distance from (8, 0) to (0, 6), which is sqrt(64 + 36) = 10. Since the radius can be 6 or 10, the relationship cannot be determined.
questions.trap: Students assume the two named points must be the ends of a diameter and answer C. Two points on a circle only pin down a chord; unless something forces that chord through the center, the radius has a floor of 6 but no ceiling.

questions.question: In the xy-plane, line p has equation y = (5/2)x - 3 and line q has equation y = -(1/2)x + c, where c is a constant. The two lines intersect at a point whose x-coordinate is 4. What is the x-intercept of line q?
questions.explanation: The intersection point lies on both lines, so its y-value can be read off line p: at x = 4, y = (5/2)(4) - 3 = 10 - 3 = 7. That gives the shared point (4, 7). Substituting it into line q gives 7 = -(1/2)(4) + c = -2 + c, so c = 9 and line q is y = -(1/2)x + 9. Setting y = 0 gives (1/2)x = 9, so x = 18.
questions.trap: Students compute c correctly and then report 9, the y-intercept, instead of the x-intercept. Others find line p's x-intercept, 6/5, having forgotten which line the question asks about. The x-intercept of q solves 0 = -(1/2)x + 9.

questions.question: In the xy-plane, several points are chosen on the line y = 1.25x + 7. If the range of the x-coordinates of those points is 12, what is the range of their y-coordinates?
questions.explanation: On a straight line, every step in x produces a step in y that is the slope times as large. Spreading the x-values over a width of 12 therefore spreads the y-values over a width of 1.25 times 12 = 15. The constant 7 shifts every point up equally and so has no effect on a range, which measures a difference. Concretely, the leftmost and rightmost chosen points differ by 12 in x, and their y-values differ by 1.25(12) = 15.
questions.trap: Students divide instead of multiplying, answering 12/1.25 = 9.6. That is the calculation you would run to go from a y-range back to an x-range. Here the x-spread is given, so the slope multiplies it.

questions.question:
In the xy-plane, a line has equation y = mx + 8, where m is a constant and 2 <= m <= 4.

Which of the following could be the x-intercept of the line?

Indicate all such values.
questions.explanation: Setting y = 0 gives 0 = mx + 8, so the x-intercept is x = -8/m. As m runs from 2 up to 4, -8/m runs from -8/2 = -4 up to -8/4 = -2, moving steadily and hitting every value in between. So the possible x-intercepts fill the interval from -4 to -2. Checking the options: -4 occurs at m = 2, -2 occurs at m = 4, and -3 occurs at m = 8/3, which lies between 2 and 4. The values -5, -1 and 2 all fall outside the interval.
questions.trap: Students test only the endpoints m = 2 and m = 4, mark -4 and -2, and leave -3 unmarked. Since m sweeps continuously through every value from 2 to 4, the x-intercept sweeps continuously through every value from -4 to -2.

questions.question:
In the xy-plane, the line y = mx + b, where m and b are constants with mb not equal to 0, has an x-intercept that is three times its y-intercept.
Column A: m
Column B: 1/3
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: The y-intercept is b, found by setting x = 0. The x-intercept is found by setting y = 0: 0 = mx + b gives x = -b/m. The condition says -b/m = 3b. Since b is not zero, divide both sides by b to get -1/m = 3, so m = -1/3. Column A is therefore -1/3, which is negative, while Column B is the positive 1/3. Column B is greater.
questions.trap: Students drop the minus sign when solving for the x-intercept, get 1/m = 3 and m = 1/3, and answer C. The x-intercept of y = mx + b is -b/m, and that negative sign is exactly what makes the slope come out negative here.

questions.question:
The figure shows triangle OAB in the xy-plane, with O the origin, A the point (0, 10) and B the point (10, 0). Point C lies on the x-axis to the right of B, and segment CD is perpendicular to the x-axis, forming triangle BCD. If BC = 4 * CD and triangles OAB and BCD have equal areas, what is the length of CD?

Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
questions.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 260" width="320" height="260" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="a" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="6" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z" fill="#1f2937"/></marker></defs><line x1="30" y1="200" x2="292" y2="200" stroke="#1f2937" fill="none" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#a)"/><line x1="56" y1="216" x2="56" y2="64" stroke="#1f2937" fill="none" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#a)"/><text x="288" y="216" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">x</text><text x="63" y="75" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">y</text><text x="50" y="217" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937" text-anchor="end">O</text><polygon points="56,200 56,120 136,200" stroke="#1f2937" fill="none" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="136,200 232,200 232,176" stroke="#1f2937" fill="none" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="56" cy="120" r="3.5" fill="#1f2937"/><text x="64" y="117" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">A (0, 10)</text><circle cx="136" cy="200" r="3.5" fill="#1f2937"/><text x="136" y="218" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937" text-anchor="middle">B</text><circle cx="232" cy="200" r="3.5" fill="#1f2937"/><text x="232" y="218" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937" text-anchor="middle">C</text><circle cx="232" cy="176" r="3.5" fill="#1f2937"/><text x="240" y="173" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">D</text></svg>
questions.explanation: Triangle OAB has legs along the axes of length 10 each, so its area is (1/2)(10)(10) = 50. Triangle BCD is also right-angled, with legs BC along the x-axis and CD vertical, so its area is (1/2)(BC)(CD). Substituting BC = 4 * CD gives (1/2)(4 * CD)(CD) = 2 * CD^2. Setting that equal to 50 gives CD^2 = 25, so CD = 5.
questions.trap: Students forget to substitute the ratio and solve (1/2)(CD)(CD) = 50, getting CD = 10. The base BC is not equal to CD; it is four times as long, and that factor of 4 is what halves the answer from 10 down to 5.

questions.question: In the xy-plane, three of the vertices of parallelogram WXYZ are W(-2, 1), X(4, -3) and Y(10, 5), as shown. What is the y-coordinate of vertex Z?
questions.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 260" width="320" height="260" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="a" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="6" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z" fill="#1f2937"/></marker></defs><path d="M62.1 234.0V26.0M111.1 234.0V26.0M160.0 234.0V26.0M208.9 234.0V26.0M257.9 234.0V26.0M49.9 209.5H270.1M49.9 160.6H270.1M49.9 111.6H270.1M49.9 62.7H270.1" stroke="#d7dee8" stroke-width="1" fill="none"/><line x1="49.9" y1="160.6" x2="270.1" y2="160.6" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#a)"/><line x1="111.1" y1="234.0" x2="111.1" y2="26.0" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#a)"/><text x="266.1" y="176.6" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">x</text><text x="118.1" y="37.0" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">y</text><text x="98.1" y="175.6" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">O</text><line x1="86.6" y1="148.4" x2="160.0" y2="197.3" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="160.0" y1="197.3" x2="233.4" y2="99.4" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="86.6" cy="148.4" r="3.5" fill="#1f2937"/><text x="79.6" y="144.4" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937" text-anchor="end">W (-2, 1)</text><circle cx="160.0" cy="197.3" r="3.5" fill="#1f2937"/><text x="162.0" y="216.3" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937" text-anchor="middle">X (4, -3)</text><circle cx="233.4" cy="99.4" r="3.5" fill="#1f2937"/><text x="227.4" y="94.4" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937" text-anchor="end">Y (10, 5)</text></svg>
questions.explanation: Naming the parallelogram WXYZ fixes the order of its vertices around the shape, so WX, XY, YZ and ZW are the four sides and WY and XZ are the two diagonals. Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so WY and XZ share a midpoint: (W + Y)/2 = (X + Z)/2, which rearranges to Z = W + Y - X. That gives Z = (-2 + 10 - 4, 1 + 5 - (-3)) = (4, 9), so the y-coordinate is 9.
questions.trap: Students treat this like an unlabelled set of three points, where three different fourth vertices are possible, and pick one of the others: W + X - Y gives (-8, -7), and X + Y - W gives (16, 1), which is why -7 and 1 both appear as options. The name WXYZ rules those out by making W and Y the ends of a diagonal.
